text: The treatment record, its terms and its approval are S2 rwb-treatment's in schema rwb_treatment and are never written in rwb_case; rwb-case consumes rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1 and rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 through its case router and holds the case route state PLAN_RUNNING and PLAN_CURE_PERIOD, the plan-timer projection row in rwb_case.timer and the durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow, with the treatment read through GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}; the event catalogue's consumer list for TreatmentApproved is read as not exhaustive and rwb-case is added to it.
why: The Ownership Map moves the treatment to S2 and keeps only the timer projection with P3, the Temporal design puts the restructure stage in TreatmentWorkflow, and the event catalogue lists rwb-comms and rwb-payment but not rwb-case as consumers of TreatmentApproved, so the seam the legacy story held in one service needs one stated reader and one stated writer.
read: ownership.json tables.treatment and tables.timer (ruling ASM-A6-tables-12); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 18, 41, 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 9 and 14; RWB-E2-004 sections 1 to 4 and 13.
confirm: Solution architect with the S2 and P3 owners in the wave 2 architecture review and the RWB-P3-E2004-CON baseline review.
impact: If S2 keeps the plan timer and the route move on its own side, the plan-timer step, the two subscriptions, one dashboard panel and one runbook entry move to S2, and the case side keeps only the projection read; no case schema or screen change.

text: The DP04 treatment product is P1 rwb-source-data's dated copy built from the treatment events and loaded by JOB-15 at 01:30 under the bank Airflow for rwb-reporting, with no data lake; the case side reads it through GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP04/records and judges staleness from the freshness element of that answer, showing the previous business date with MSG-P1-001, and writes no row of it.
why: The legacy story owned the extract step inside P3, the target job map gives JOB-15 to rwb-reporting with an Airflow trigger and no data lake, the Ownership Map gives dp_treatment to P1, and no source names the case-facing read path or the freshness element the story's AC3 and AC10 need.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (JOB-15, 01:30, rwb-reporting, Airflow trigger, no data lake) and slides 37 and 41; ownership.json tables.dp_treatment (asm ASM-A6-tables-14) and tables.lake_copy_watermark (asm ASM-A6-tables-13); RWB-E2-004 section 4 step 10 and section 12.
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2004-APP 12.2, 12.8, 5 (X7) and 19; RWB-P3-E2004-CON 12.2 and AC5; RWB-P3-E2004-OPS 12.2, 13 (alert mapping) and 19
confirm: Data product owner with the P1 and P9 owners, at the RWB-P3-E2004-CON baseline review and the UAT run.
impact: If P1 publishes another read path or another freshness element, one consumed row, one client adapter and one fake change; the DP04 columns and the derived status stay the product owner's; no schema, event or workflow change in rwb-case.

text: The plan timers of GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers carry treatmentId, timerType INSTALLMENT_DUE or CURE_PERIOD, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused and status, every one of them optional within major version 1, with expiresAt as an offset date-time in the Asia/Bangkok zone and the array ordered by expiresAt ascending; no rule ID and no package version is returned in the timers answer, and they are read from the decision log instead.
why: The projection row and its columns exist, LOV-TIMER already holds the two plan types, and the operation is in the map, but no source fixes the JSON properties, their optionality or the zone convention, and three consumers plus the wave 2 harness read the same answer.
read: ownership.json api 'GET /cases/{caseId}/timers' and tables.timer (asm ASM-A6-tables-12); TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-044) and T3.2 (LOV-TIMER, LOV-TIMER-STATUS); RWB-E2-004 sections 11 and 12.
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2004-APP 12.1 and 12.8; RWB-P3-E2004-CON 11 and AC2; RWB-P3-E2004-OPS 12.1
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case with the timer owner (RWB-P3-E1028-CON) and the wave 2 harness, in the RWB-P3-E2004-CON baseline review.
impact: A property addition is additive within version 1 and costs one schema line, one fake fixture and one contract test; requiring rule ID or version in the answer would add one projection column and one migration step instead.

text: The operational values are provisional until UAT: the projection lag alerts above 5 minutes, a subscription lag alerts above 500 events or 10 minutes of consumer lag, the .dlt count alerts on any event, the exception-queue count of refused plan steps alerts above 10 open cases, and the DP04 treatment product alerts when its last loaded business date is more than one day behind.
why: No source gives a threshold, a window or a band, and the deployment cannot ship without an alert value; every value stays a values-file entry and never a code constant or a business parameter.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28 and 44; Template and Rules R7.2 s17; RWB-E2-004 section 5 X6 (retry 3 times) and section 13 (consumer retry limit 3, NFR-026).
confirm: DevOps lead with the rwb-case service owner at UAT, and the platform observability owner for the lag and band definitions.
impact: A threshold change is a values-file change and one runbook line; no code, contract, schema or workflow change.
